claims.text: The dynamic mechanical behavior of solidified Co-free FeNiCrMn is governed by transient deformation-induced short-range ordering clusters.
Deformation-induced SRO formation in FeNiCrMn is reversible.
Transient SRO clusters dynamically pin dislocations in FeNiCrMn.
At cryogenic temperatures and high strain rates, SRO forms readily and remains sufficiently stable to enhance yield strength and strain hardening.
At elevated temperatures, thermal activation dissolves SRO and reduces dynamic strengthening.
Controlled casting followed by homogenization produces a uniform, equiaxed FCC FeNiCrMn microstructure.
Rapid dislocation motion under dynamic loading triggers local atomic rearrangements that create transient SRO clusters.
SRO-related local chemical structure can interact with dislocations and contribute to strengthening in FCC high- or medium-entropy alloys.
Impediment of dislocation glide by SRO clusters enhances local strain hardening and yield strength in FeNiCrMn.
Thermal fluctuations at high temperature overcome the ordering energy of SRO clusters.
Low-temperature, high-strain-rate strengthening should correlate with detectable SRO signatures in synchrotron XRD and TEM.
Weakening or absence of SRO at high temperature should coincide with lower dynamic hardening.
Intermediate-temperature, quasi-static conditions are expected to produce minimal transient SRO formation.
The proposed mechanism is bounded to controlled, solidified, equiaxed, single-phase FCC Co-free FeNiCrMn.
Compositional variation, multiphase microstructures, and different processing histories may introduce competing reinforcing mechanisms.
Twinning, transformation-induced plasticity, and phonon drag may be competing deformation mechanisms at extreme temperatures or strain rates.
In Co-containing NiCrFeCoMn, a high-strain-rate yield-strength increase has been attributed to phonon drag rather than SRO.
A consistent failure of SRO evolution to correlate with yield strength and strain hardening would falsify the proposed mechanism.
